title: Container query units
learningObjectives: Explain container query units and apply it to responsive components.

understand.concept: Container query units size values relative to a query container. cqw and cqh represent percentages of the query container's width and height; cqi and cqb relate to its inline and block dimensions; cqmin and cqmax use the smaller or larger relevant dimension.
understand.whyItMatters: These units can size typography and spacing based on a component's own container. Ensure the intended ancestor establishes the query container, otherwise fallback viewport-relative behaviour may be used.
understand.analogy: Container query units use the component's own workspace as the ruler.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; media and container queries use formal CSS conditions and sizing references.

explain.narrative: The padding and heading size respond to the inline size of the query container.

practise.guidedTask: Compare cqi with vw by placing the same component in two containers of different widths on one viewport.
practise.independentTask: Build a reusable component and test it at different viewport and container sizes, with long labels and text enlargement.
hints: Inspect the actual query condition and container.
Test just below and above thresholds.
Keep content and keyboard order logical.

questions.prompt: Which container unit is based on the query container's inline size?
questions.explanation: cqi is one percent of the query container's inline size.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable responsive test?
options: Test different widths and content lengths
Test only at one standard phone size
questions.answer: Test different widths and content lengths
questions.explanation: Responsive behaviour depends on actual space and content, not just a device label.
